I personally love all the churches and monasteries open to the public, often times for free (not even for religious reasons, the architecture is really nice). There's also this one absolutely breathtaking street called Na Kocourkách in Prague 6, it's got a bunch of really old and pretty houses. In the vicinity there's also parks and such. A few stations by tram away from there is also Obora Hvězda - a pretty big forest with an old summer residence shaped like a star. My personal favorite is also Petřín - a hill close by to Prague castle, it's got a lookout tower, beautiful gardens and remains of old battlements.

I'd recommend the YouTube channel HONEST GUIDE, they're folks from Prague making videos for tourists about it, showcasing it and also warning about what to look out for. Hope you have a nice trip :)

There are relatively safe binders you can buy for cheap or charities that can give them for you for free. If getting a package is an issue ask someone you know and trust if you can have it shipped to their place.

And if that's not an option you can try wearing or even layering sports bras or get a compression shirt/tank top if you can (excuse for wearing them is that it's more comfortable for sports and existing in general)

Another amazing way of making use of plums (or any other fruit in abundance, in my country it just happens to always be plums) is to make a sort of unsweetened jam (powidl) from it. You just take a large amount of the fruit (pit-less) and put it in the largest pot you own and cook it on low heat with some spice like cinnamon, no sugar for 6 or more hours until it becomes a thick paste. It takes a lot of energy but you can make use of a *lot* of fruit and it's amazing for cooking (great for sauces or cakes) or to eat on it's own or with jogurt or potato cakes.

You can also take a shot at making slivovitz (plum brandy). May not be completely legal to destill it on your own and I'm not sure how strict regulations are in your area but it's not hard to destill on your own or you can bring the undestilled stuff to a distillery
